- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above immediate prior peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to counteract downward bias.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, adjust downward by 1–3%.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% in first 3–5 days of sentiment change.
- If forecast shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising days) but sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce slope by 10–20% to avoid overconfidence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5–7 days), model often misses it; reduce first 3–5 forecast values by 2–5% to align with observed mean reversion.
